secondary.title: Profiles and proportions
secondary.copy: Horizontal siding and vertical board-and-batten create different patterns across a wall. Consider exposure, corner details, window trim and transitions before selecting a profile.

secondary.title: Color and matching details
secondary.copy: Look at full-size samples outdoors and compare them with roofing, windows and masonry. Review the manufacturer’s color matrix for the chosen siding and coordinate soffit, trim and accessories rather than relying on a screen image.

secondary.title: Specifications to confirm
secondary.copy: Ask for the exact product-line specification, fastening instructions, wind-performance documentation and applicable warranty. A brand name alone does not identify a panel’s thickness, performance or installation requirements.

cards.title: LP SmartSide
cards.description: Explore the brand’s material options, design considerations and documentation to discuss with Roof King.

secondary.title: Build a coordinated exterior
secondary.copy: Start with the main siding profile, then consider accent areas and matching trim. Lap siding, vertical panels and shakes produce different visual rhythms; use them deliberately around entryways, gables and larger wall areas.

secondary.title: Primed or prefinished
secondary.copy: LP offers primed and ExpertFinish prefinished siding options. Ask which finishes and textures are available for the selected profile, review physical samples, and discuss paint and maintenance responsibilities as part of the project scope.

secondary.title: Installation and maintenance
secondary.copy: Confirm clearance, flashing, fastening and finishing requirements for the exact product. Engineered wood still requires installation and care according to manufacturer instructions. Review product-specific warranties instead of assuming every item in the family has identical coverage.

secondary.title: Choose the siding profile
secondary.copy: Lap siding creates a horizontal pattern that can work with a range of home styles. Discuss the visible exposure, surface texture and treatment of gables and accent areas, along with trim widths and corner details.

secondary.title: Coordinate the finish
secondary.copy: Review current manufacturer finish options for the chosen product and region. Compare samples in daylight with existing brick, stone, roof colors and windows. Ask what is factory finished, what requires field painting, and how future touch-ups will be handled.

secondary.title: Review the complete assembly
secondary.copy: Siding performance depends on more than the face material. Confirm flashing, clearances, fastening and water-management details against the applicable manufacturer instructions. Check the exact warranty and care guidance for the selected product and finish.

cards.title: Trex
cards.description: Explore the brand’s material options, design considerations and documentation to discuss with Roof King.

secondary.title: Compare decking collections
secondary.copy: Review the current Trex collections and physical samples for color and grain. Consider the deck’s sun exposure, barefoot use, furniture and traffic. Surface temperature and the way a board looks outdoors are useful questions to resolve before choosing a color.

secondary.title: Complete the outdoor space
secondary.copy: Coordinate railing, stair details and lighting with the deck layout. Confirm which accessories suit the selected system and how they attach. The framing and support structure need their own assessment; new boards alone do not establish that an existing deck is sound.

secondary.title: Care and product documentation
secondary.copy: Check cleaning guidance, required board spacing, approved fasteners and the exact product warranty. Composite decking has different care requirements from wood. Do not transfer a warranty length or performance claim from one collection to another.
